info.title: Ledger API
info.description: A double-entry ledger. Amounts are decimal strings, never JSON numbers; posting ids are strings because a bigserial outruns `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`; timestamps are ISO 8601 with an offset. Balances are derived from postings and are never stored.

baseCurrency.description: An ISO 4217 code, such as EUR.

role.description: The caller's role in this book. Present so the UI can stop offering what the policy forbids - a viewer should not be shown a compose button that always ends in a 403. The server still decides; this only lets the client stop asking.

currency.description: An ISO 4217 code, such as EUR.

parentId.description: Null for a root account. The tree the frontend draws is built from this column.

reversedBy.description: The reversal of this entry, where one exists. The inverse of `reversalOf`, and the only way a caller can know an entry is already reversed without attempting the reversal and reading `ENTRY_ALREADY_REVERSED` off the failure.

amount.description: A decimal string. Never a JSON number: a JSON number is an IEEE 754 double.

currency.description: An ISO 4217 code, such as EUR.

asOf.description: The instant asked for, or null for the balance as of now.

balance.description: A decimal string. Never a JSON number: a JSON number is an IEEE 754 double.

currency.description: An ISO 4217 code, such as EUR.

debits.description: A decimal string. Never a JSON number: a JSON number is an IEEE 754 double.

credits.description: A decimal string. Never a JSON number: a JSON number is an IEEE 754 double.

balanced.description: False means this book does not add up, which is a fact about the data, not a query error.

amount.description: A decimal string. Never a JSON number: a JSON number is an IEEE 754 double.

runningBalance.description: The account balance through this posting, computed by the server.

currency.description: An ISO 4217 code, such as EUR.

nextCursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page. Null on the last one.

prefix.description: The leading segment of the token, stored so a key can be identified in a list.

token.description: The plaintext key. Returned once, here, and never again: what is stored is a SHA-256 hash, so there is nothing left to show on a later request.

Problem.description: RFC 9457 Problem Details. `code` is the stable identifier a client should branch on; `requestId` is echoed in `X-Request-Id` and is what finds the failure in the logs.

type.description: An identifier, not a URL to fetch.

errors.description: Field-level detail, on validation failures only.

bearerAuth.description: Either a JWT access token from `/auth/login`, or an API key issued by `POST /books/{bookId}/api-keys`. Both are presented as `Authorization: Bearer <value>`; a key is recognised by its `lk_` prefix.

refreshCookie.name: refresh_token
refreshCookie.description: Set by the auth endpoints, httpOnly, scoped to `/auth`. Never readable by a script, which is the reason the short-lived access token is the one that lives in memory.
